priorStories.headline: Man charged in alleged Mall of America plot
priorStories.body:
Federal prosecutors charged 18-year-old Sheikhdoon Abdullahi Mohamud with receiving a firearm and ammunition to commit a federal terrorism crime. They allege that he planned an ISIS-inspired mass shooting at the Mall of America on October 24.

The FBI arrested Mohamud on October 6 after an undercover transaction involving an inert rifle. He made his initial court appearance October 7. The allegations have not been adjudicated.

priorStories.headline: Russian barrage kills at least 28 in Ukraine
priorStories.body:
Russian missile and drone attacks across Ukraine killed at least 28 people and injured about 100, according to a late update from Ukraine’s interior minister.

The largest reported loss was in Pryluky, where a missile destroyed a residential building. Ukrainian officials also reported damage to energy and industrial facilities. Russia said it targeted military-industrial sites.

sources.name: Office of the President of Ukraine

priorStories.headline: Attacks on Saudi airports kill three people
priorStories.body:
Attacks on Abha International Airport and Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport killed three foreign residents and injured 36 people, according to Saudi aviation authorities.

The Abha attack occurred October 6. The Riyadh attack on October 7 killed a Sudanese resident. Saudi authorities did not assign responsibility, while Yemen’s Houthi movement claimed the attacks.

candidates.summary: Police used tear gas after students erected barricades outside the Hélène Boucher high school in northeastern Paris during continuing protests over school funding and conditions. France’s Education Ministry said 375 schools were fully or partially closed Thursday, while the Interior Ministry said more than 6,600 arrests had been made since the protests began in late September.
candidates.title: French school protests continue with Paris clashes

candidates.summary: The British government said its consulate-general building in Jerusalem would remain open but operate as the UK Mission, Jerusalem, after discussions with Israel. Britain temporarily withdrew some staff and families and said it would not retaliate while talks continued. Israel said the site had ceased functioning as a consulate and that 20 British diplomats would leave, while seven would remain with limited duties.
candidates.title: Britain downgrades Jerusalem consulate to mission

candidates.summary: Hurricane Isaias intensified over the Gulf, reaching maximum sustained winds of 80 mph by the National Hurricane Center’s 0900 UTC advisory. Forecasters expected further strengthening before a projected landfall along the northern U.S. Gulf Coast late Friday or early Saturday and warned of dangerous storm surge, damaging winds and flooding.
candidates.title: Hurricane Isaias intensifies in Gulf

candidates.summary: The Swedish Academy awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature to Canadian poet, essayist and translator Anne Carson, citing her genre-crossing body of work and engagement with classical traditions. Carson’s books include “Autobiography of Red,” “Eros the Bittersweet” and translations of ancient Greek literature.
candidates.title: Anne Carson wins Nobel Prize in Literature

candidates.summary: A man carrying a gun was fatally shot by security personnel at the federal courthouse in downtown Nashville, police said. Federal authorities took charge of the investigation because the shooting occurred on federal property. Officials had not released the man’s identity or additional circumstances by the end of the coverage interval.
candidates.title: Armed man fatally shot at Nashville federal courthouse

candidates.summary: Hurricane Isaias strengthened as it approached the northern U.S. Gulf Coast. Authorities ordered mandatory evacuations in parts of Florida, and Alabama declared emergencies as forecasters warned of life-threatening storm surge, tornadoes, damaging winds and flooding.
candidates.title: Hurricane Isaias prompts Gulf Coast evacuations
candidates.geography: Gulf of Mexico; Florida; Alabama, United States

candidates.summary: President Donald Trump said the United States would not resume military strikes against Iran before the November 3 midterm elections. He said discussions with Iran were productive while the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports remained in effect.
candidates.title: Trump says US will not strike Iran before midterms

candidates.summary: The National Hurricane Center said Isaias strengthened to a Category 2 hurricane with maximum sustained winds of 105 mph at 10 p.m. CDT. Storm-surge and hurricane warnings remained in effect along parts of the northern Gulf Coast, where evacuations and preparations were underway.
candidates.title: Hurricane Isaias strengthens to Category 2
candidates.geography: Gulf of Mexico; United States Gulf Coast

candidates.summary: Heavy rain caused flash floods and mudslides in Santiago, sweeping away vehicles, flooding homes and prompting evacuations. Authorities reported at least six injuries, and firefighters said they rescued or evacuated more than 1,000 people. President José Antonio Kast declared an emergency in Las Condes after the Mapocho River overflowed.
candidates.title: Floods and mudslides hit Santiago

candidates.summary: The National Hurricane Center said Tropical Storm Simon became a hurricane over the eastern Pacific, with maximum sustained winds of 75 mph at 9 p.m. CST. The storm was about 235 miles south of Manzanillo, Mexico, and hurricane warnings covered portions of the southwestern and west-central Mexican coast.
candidates.title: Simon becomes hurricane off Mexico

candidates.summary: A Russian guided bomb struck near two passenger buses in Kramatorsk, killing at least 30 people and wounding 18, according to Ukrainian regional authorities. Later reporting citing Ukraine’s emergency service put the death toll at 33. Public transportation was suspended in Kramatorsk and Sloviansk after the attack.
candidates.title: Russian bomb strikes passenger buses in Kramatorsk

candidates.summary: A U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer shot and wounded a Dominican man in the neck during an arrest operation in New York City, officials said. A 5-year-old boy was inside the man’s car and was unharmed. Federal authorities did not provide a detailed account of what led to the officer firing.
candidates.title: ICE officer wounds man in New York City shooting
candidates.geography: New York City, New York, United States

candidates.summary: The Trump administration announced that Microsoft, Adobe and six technology and outsourcing firms would be suspended from the Permanent Labor Certification program, which employers use to sponsor foreign workers for permanent residency. Officials alleged abuse and fraud; the action did not suspend the H-1B visa program or establish that the allegations had been proven.
candidates.title: US suspends technology firms from worker green-card program
